En 1891, Georg Cantor publie l'argument: In 1891, Georg Cantor publishes the diagonal argument. Suppose a list of all infinite sequences of 0s and 1s. Build a new sequence by changing the first digit of the first, the second of the second, and so on: it differs from every sequence on the list. So no list can be complete. There are infinities larger than that of the whole numbers: the real numbers are one.

À Londres, chaque semaine, des bulletins: In London, every week, bills of mortality listed the dead and their causes of death. John Graunt, a haberdasher, combed through them patiently and in 1662 published his Natural and Political Observations. The bills did not record the age of the dead; yet, by reasoning alone, he drew up the first life table. With the backing of King Charles II, the Royal Society admitted him that same year.
